evidence.fact: Commercial AI record-retrieval platforms for law firms say they automate authorization validation, sending requests to US providers, follow-up, and sorting the records that come back. They also connect to case-management tools like Clio. These are vendor claims and say human oversight is still needed.

Releasing medical records needs a HIPAA authorization signed by the patient or a qualified personal representative, or else a subpoena or court order. A human has to supply this step, and an attorney cannot sign it just because they are on the case.

Retrieval guides for lawyers say the process starts only once a HIPAA-compliant authorization, subpoena, or court order is in place. After that, requests go to each provider's records department and have to be followed up until the records arrive.

Commercial retail space-planning software (LEAFIO) builds planograms automatically from sales data, ABC analysis, turnover and user-defined rules, and auto-calculates facings. These are vendor claims.
DotActiv markets AI planogram generation with batch creation of size variants that follow layout rules, plus an LLM category-management assistant. These are vendor claims.

Retail layouts are bound by occupancy, egress width and travel-distance code rules, such as the 75-ft sprinklered mercantile limit cited from IBC Table 1006.2.1 in a practitioner forum. A human with knowledge of the actual site still has to check compliance and fit before the layout is built in the store.

Commercial EHS platforms such as Notify Spark (launched October 2025), Benchmark Gensuite and EHS4Safety already use AI to handle accident reports, root-cause analysis and workers' compensation workflows. That covers the documentation, analysis and reporting steps.

Employers must collect information from injured employees, witnesses and treating health professionals and finish OSHA Form 301 within 7 days. An employer's designated representative can complete the form, so the law does not appear to require a specific licensed signer. The accident-scene inspection and in-person witness interviews still need a human on site.

A state workers' compensation report can count as an equivalent form if it captures the required information. That lets an agent draft one report that covers both the insurer and OSHA filings from the facts it gathers.

Pactum's AI chatbot runs supplier negotiations with Walmart's long-tail vendors on its own, within a value function that analysts define. Results go straight into ERP/CRM, and 3 out of 4 suppliers said they preferred it to a human. Its scope is still limited to commodity items, though.

In 2026, agentic procurement tools from Pactum, Keelvar, Arkestro and SAP Ariba contact and negotiate with hundreds of suppliers at once inside preset guardrails. Strategic contracts and escalations stay under human review.

Vendors and analysts describe tiered oversight: agents act alone on low-value spend, while a person picks among options for strategic sourcing and records why. That fits partial delegation rather than full delegation.

Agentic AI in hotels is being used to coordinate housekeeping scheduling, guest requests, distribution and revenue management. Agents can query the property management system and open maintenance tickets, but only about 1 in 10 chains uses agents at scale, and the specific savings figures come from vendor blogs.

Vendor material says agents check the property management system in real time and either answer a request or start a workflow such as a maintenance ticket. Inspecting and fixing the problem is still left to staff on site.
Lodging manager job postings include physically inspecting the facility, rooms and grounds, doing preventive maintenance, landscaping and overseeing check-in and check-out.

A 2025 WSP case study presented at IAIA describes an AI workflow for environmental baseline studies. It flags outdated datasets, fills gaps with remote sensing and uses text and data mining. This shows that agents can do the desk-based design and data-gathering steps.

A November 2025 ISEP advice note says AI adoption in environmental impact assessment is still uneven. A June 2026 UK scoping report includes a statement disclosing its AI use. Together they show AI assisting EIA scoping while practitioners keep responsibility for the work.

Under US agency NEPA rules, such as the Interior rule at 43 CFR 46.107, a Responsible Official must independently evaluate contractor-prepared environmental work, give written concurrence and remain responsible for the documents. A human therefore has to review and sign off.

UT Austin's open-source AI-assisted cataloging project builds metadata from images of items, searches OCLC WorldCat for matching records and has an LLM score each match. Catalogers still review the matches before batch upload, so a human stays in the loop.
OCLC already uses machine learning at scale on WorldCat bibliographic records. It ran AI de-duplication of records in 2025 and later extended it to all formats and languages.

A May 2026 industry post (secondary source) says OCLC added AI suggestions for classification and subject headings to Record Manager and Connexion, saving up to about 20 minutes per title in pilots. It also says OCLC's Bibliographic Formats and Standards now explains how to record AI-generated metadata, which implies human oversight.
Pharmacy software already produces the reorder lists from PAR or min/max levels. That covers the digital step before restocking but not putting stock on the shelves.
In this job description, aides restock shelves throughout the pharmacy and refill supplies to set inventory levels. Both are hands-on duties done under pharmacist supervision.
O*NET lists restocking storage areas and replenishing shelves as a separate task from receiving and inventorying medications.

Kitchen display system (KDS) expo screens only handle the information side of the hand-off. They flag front-of-house staff when all items in an order are done, but a person still carries the plates to the pass.
Expo screens list each dish as it finishes so servers don't have to check whether it is ready. That covers the coordination messages, not the physical passing of food.
Kitchen staff mark items done by 'bumping' them on the KDS, which tells servers the food is ready. The software tracks status but never moves the food.
Toast's help article describes the server printing an itemized receipt and leaving it with the guest. Guests can also view the itemized check on their phone, so the POS already builds the check.
Voice AI ordering agents connect to POS systems such as Toast, Square and Clover. They send captured orders and modifiers into the POS, where pricing and totals are handled.
With QR ordering, guests add items straight onto the same check in the POS, so no server has to enter them. Splitting checks and printing them happen on the floor.

Payment at restaurant tables is being automated by dedicated pay-at-table hardware such as NCR Voyix Aloha Pay-At-Table and the tabletop kiosks Chili's uses. These are fixed systems that replace the task, not a general AI agent doing the worker's job.

Self-checkout and self-order kiosks with AI features, such as Partner Tech's Paula, need physical card terminals or tabletop devices. Accepting payment at the counter means being there in person to handle cash, cards and receipts, which a software-only agent cannot do. It can only help with the digital steps in the POS system.

Vendor reports say 66% of US consumers prefer self-service kiosks to staffed checkouts (a figure from the vendor itself). This shows how payment is moving to kiosks rather than to agents running the register.

Digital tools automate developmental screening steps such as ASQ-3 delivery and scoring, and there are AI video-based screening apps for parents. But screening flags still need professional judgement and are meant to start a conversation, not stand alone.

Childcare programs use ASQ to identify developmental and social-emotional concerns, and it depends on adults directly observing the child. An agent can score the questionnaires or draft messages, but it cannot watch children in the room.

Childcare providers are mandated reporters for abuse. Developmental concerns are raised with parents through direct conversations, meetings, email or phone, which is a trust-based, in-person part of the job.

Caregiver apps such as Daily Nanny produce daily and weekly reports from logged naps, feeds, diapers and activities. These can support a parent check-in, but the nanny still has to log the data and hold the conversation.

Kidscare AI advertises AI journaling and milestone tagging to improve communication with parents about a child's development. This helps with preparation, but the content still comes from the caregiver's own firsthand observations.
Some systems, such as MyKidReports, generate the daily report automatically at checkout. That automates written updates, not the regular two-way meeting in which a nanny and parents build trust.
BLS says recreation workers do hands-on work such as setting up equipment, helping participants during activities, and cleaning and maintaining equipment or facilities.
O*NET lists 'Provide for entertainment and set up related decorations and equipment' as one of the occupation's tasks.

AI tools can suggest themes, decor concepts, checklists and shopping lists, which covers only the planning part. Hanging decorations, setting up equipment and running the entertainment still need a person on site.

Conversational AI agents can already sell event tickets end to end in chat. They recommend events, handle seat selection and run checkout for venues and ticketing platforms. This covers remote or digital sales channels only, not the counter.

AI agents are expected to automate ticket-buying steps such as queueing for ticket releases, comparing prices and making the purchase. The digital transaction side of selling tickets can be automated.

2026 AI customer-service agents can understand what the customer wants, pull account data and carry out actions such as payments and refunds within the conversation. At a cashier's counter, a person still has to take cash, hand over printed tickets or goods and scan items, which needs a physical presence.

Riff describes an agent that finds open purchase orders with no supplier confirmation, sends follow-ups to suppliers on its own, updates the ERP (SAP S/4HANA, Oracle, Dynamics 365) and escalates to a buyer when a supplier doesn't respond. This is the vendor's own claim and has not been tested independently.

Fellowmind describes a Supplier Communication Agent that sorts incoming supplier emails into confirmations, change requests and rejections, then shows the proposed ERP changes to a person for review before applying them. So changes still need a human step. This is the vendor's own claim and has not been tested independently.

SAP says Lemvigh-Müller's agents read supplier responses and compare quantities, dates and prices against purchase orders in SAP Cloud ERP. Mismatches are sent to follow-up workflows or flagged for a buyer to review. This is a customer story published by the vendor, with no independent measured results.
Stayntouch says its PMS sends a room's 'dirty' status to housekeepers' mobile devices when the folio closes at checkout, and then assigns cleaning tasks automatically. This is a vendor claim.
Oracle OPERA's documentation describes a setting that changes a room's housekeeping status automatically at checkout, so front desk staff don't have to set it by hand.

Mews MakeUpMyRoom reorders the housekeeping queue as soon as a checkout is logged in Mews. This is a vendor claim. Remaining cases, such as guests who leave without checking out, may still need a staff member to confirm the room is empty.

Libraries already run chatbots that point users to databases, help them search the catalog and answer questions about library services. Examples are Ask ALEX at the University of Oklahoma and ELIZA at Mahasarakham University. They are available around the clock, but no independent study has checked how accurate they are.

Job specifications say library assistants greet and help patrons at a front counter or public desk and show them where library services and materials are. Much of this instruction happens in person, on site.
No licence or certification is needed. Postings ask for a high school diploma plus experience, so no law requires a human to do or sign off on the task.

Vendors describe AI receptionists that answer calls, work out why the person is calling, apply routing rules and connect them to the right person, team or queue. They hand the call to a human when the caller asks or when the AI can't help. These sources are vendor marketing, and no independent accuracy benchmarks were found.

Virtual reception systems check visitors in and alert the host by SMS, email or chat. When a case is more complex, they connect the visitor to a live receptionist by video. This means walk-in visitors still partly need a human or physical kiosk hardware.
AI front-desk products say they welcome and verify visitors and notify hosts automatically at check-in, while sources note that AI still struggles to show empathy to stressed or confused visitors.

Prepress systems such as Enfocus PitStop Server already ingest files without a person: they watch hot folders, check incoming PDFs against preflight profiles and sort them into pass and fail folders with reports. Switch can also pull jobs from email, FTP and cloud services.
Kodak Prinergy ships Smart Hot Folder setups that are fully or semi-automatic for bringing jobs into the prepress workflow.

In 2026, computer-use agents can operate desktop apps with mouse and keyboard to enter and move data. This covers the keyboard and mouse part of the task, but someone still has to place physical originals on the scanner or in front of the camera.

A Morgan Lewis analysis from 2026 says AI agents are coming into labor relations work but will not replace labor negotiators or employee relations professionals. Unions are also pushing back on algorithmic management and bargaining over its use.
UK legal guidance in 2026 says AI can support HR and management decisions on grievances but should not replace human judgement. Acas is consulting on whether its grievance code should cover AI use.

Under the NLRA, meetings with employees and union representatives come with legal representation rights (Weingarten). These are person-to-person dealings between management and labor, not document processing.
O*NET lists this as a core hand-packer task: mark and label containers, container tags, or products using marking tools, alongside physical handling duties such as forklifts and pallet jacks.

Label printing software already designs labels, fills in their data from WMS, ERP or e-commerce systems, and prints them automatically from triggers or APIs. A software agent could therefore handle the digital part (label content and printing), but a person or a print-and-apply machine still has to put the label on the item.
SHRM's hand packer job description treats marking and labeling as manual physical work. Standard sources mention no licence or sign-off requirement for this task.

O*NET lists 'Load materials and products into package processing equipment' as a task for Packers and Packagers, Hand (53-7064.00). The occupation is defined as packing or packaging a wide variety of products and materials by hand, which is physical manipulation work.

The occupation's related tasks are also physical (examining, weighing, sealing and labeling containers). The reference agent has no robotics, so it can do at most minor digital support like looking up loading specs, not a substantial part of the task.

Batesville's Family Choices Digital Showroom is an online tool that guides families through choosing burial and cremation products. It suggests products based on information gathered in conversation, shows choices in real-time 3D and links to ordering. Software can therefore present product information without a person, but it does not maintain the physical casket display.

Funeral home software such as Passare and the tools listed on Capterra includes product catalogs that can be shared online and online arrangement features. One funeral director said these tools are not easy to use for showing caskets in the arrangement room, which suggests in-person showing is still the norm.

The FTC Funeral Rule requires funeral homes to give a General Price List to anyone who asks about goods, services or prices in person. They must also offer a casket price list before showing caskets, and give accurate prices to people who ask by phone. The rule sets how the information must be disclosed, but it does not require a licensed person to give it.

The funeral director normally gathers pallbearers 10–20 minutes before the service for an in-person rehearsal. During the service the director cues them aloud or by gesture and shows them where to place their hands when loading the casket. This on-site part needs a physical presence that an AI agent can't provide.

Funeral home case-management and family-portal software, such as Passare, Procession and Tukios, already handles scheduling and sends arrangement updates and notifications. An agent could use these tools to recruit and confirm pallbearers and send them written instructions. I found no feature built specifically for pallbearers.
Funeral-home guides describe the director as the person who instructs pallbearers. None of the sources say a licence or law requires a licensed person to arrange or brief them.

Affirmative action plan software already handles the data collection, analysis and reporting for equal-opportunity compliance, such as flagging underrepresentation and tracking progress toward goals. These analytic and drafting sub-steps can be done digitally. The source is a low-authority page.

Under 41 CFR 60-2, as of the 2022 legal alerts, covered US federal contractors had to certify through OFCCP's registration portal that they had developed and maintained their affirmative action programs. The results do not name the signatory, but the certification is an organizational legal representation, which points to a human accountability step. Whether the requirement still applies in 2026 was not confirmed; it was not verified here, but EO 11246 was reportedly revoked in January 2025, which would reduce this barrier.
The EEOC has warned that using AI does not excuse employers from liability for employment decisions. That makes human review of AI-generated appraisal and equity programs necessary before use.

O*NET lists 'Perform minor repairs and routine cleaning of audio and video equipment' as a core task for Audio and Video Technicians. Next to it is 'Notify supervisors when major equipment repairs are needed', so the work is hands-on upkeep of physical gear.
AI-assisted AV monitoring platforms analyze incidents and logs, suggest fixes and automate approved remote workflows. They help with diagnosis but cannot clean equipment or make physical repairs.

Remote AV monitoring gives per-device telemetry (lamp hours, power state, input errors) and remote commands. The vendor claims this cuts unnecessary on-site visits, but a technician still has to go on site to fix physical faults.

Broadcast automation systems commonly have a traffic or scheduling layer that builds program logs and feeds a playout layer that produces as-run logs. This means scheduling and reading logs is already digital, structured work done in software.
Aiir Scheduler can generate and export up to 30 days of music logs automatically, so log scheduling is already largely automated.

Playout vendors sell AI-driven scheduling that recommends the order of content. This is vendor marketing, but it shows the sub-steps are machine-executable. Final on-air and recording decisions and handling last-minute changes still usually need a technician in the control room to review them.

A global survey of practice found that contact lens application and removal training sessions took a median of 30 minutes. Lenses were usually dispensed only after the instructor watched the patient apply and remove them successfully three times. This is hands-on, in-person supervision.

Nevada requires dispensing optician applicants to log 15 hours of insertion and removal training on a record signed by a supervisor. The UK College of Optometrists requires a witness to confirm that a trainee can insert and remove a lens on a patient's eye safely. Both make this a licensed, physical competency.

Some AI tools already cover parts of the task. J&J Vision's 'Andy' chatbot answers questions about insertion, removal and lens care. The 'Lensie' app says it uses camera tracking to give real-time coaching on insertion. That claim comes from the developer and has not been validated.

O*NET lists 'Clean and organize work area and disinfect equipment after treatment' as a core task for Physical Therapist Aides (31-2022.00). Related tasks include changing linens and setting up equipment, which are also hands-on physical work.

APTA guidance says to clean all equipment, devices and surfaces between patients, following CDC disinfection recommendations. This means wiping physical surfaces at the point of care, which a software-only agent cannot do. An agent could at most look up the disinfection steps or keep the cleaning log.

Under infection-control manuals, shared equipment is disinfected at the point of care between each use, following the manufacturer's instructions. No law requires a licensed person to do this work, but it must be done in person.

O*NET lists the task as 'Assist patients to dress, undress, or put on and remove supportive devices, such as braces, splints, or slings.' Aides do it under close supervision of a physical therapist or physical therapy assistant, which means hands-on physical help with patients who may be injured.
A state job specification lists 'assist patients with dressing and undressing; apply and remove braces and splints' among the aide's in-person patient-care duties.

An employer job posting describes aides removing and replacing braces, splints and slings on patients' bodies before and after treatment. This is direct physical work that a software-only agent cannot do.

O*NET lists offering assistance to mourners as they enter or exit limousines as a Funeral Attendant task. The same profile includes other hands-on duties such as driving funeral vehicles and supervising processions.
SHRM's sample job description says attendants help mourners into and out of limousines, funeral vehicles and other transportation. This is done in person, physically and with compassion.
Alberta's occupational profile says the role has physical demands, including heavy lifting of over 50 kg.

Consumer AI climbing apps such as Climbah, Bouldering AI: Coach and MoveCl say they analyze uploaded videos for body position, foot placement and technique, and give feedback and training plans. That helps with coaching. Showing a skill in person, checking harnesses and knots, and spotting a climber still need a human on site. These capabilities come from app store listings and have not been independently verified.

MoveCl's listing says it detects 28 climbing techniques with pose estimation and scores them against ideal form. This shows AI can help with feedback on technique, but it cannot give hands-on instruction or demonstrate equipment.

Forum posts (not authoritative) say AMGA certification is not legally required in the US. They also say insurers and land permits in practice expect certified or vouched-for guides, so liability for the safety of people being taught sits with a human guide. I did not confirm any statute.
Crafco's Model 30 pavement router is a walk-behind machine. A worker on site steers it by an adjustable handle, and an electric clutch starts and stops the cutter-head.
A Cimline patent says the router operator has to keep raising and lowering the cutting bits when moving between random cracks. Doing this task means handling the machine by hand in real time.

Marathon's CR250KL crack router is a 20-25 hp engine-driven machine with carbide router blades. It is field equipment run by a person on the pavement and has no software interface that an agent could operate remotely.

O*NET lists this task for Highway Maintenance Workers (47-4051.00). Related duties include driving heavy equipment and vehicles with attachments to sweep debris from paved surfaces, and setting out signs and cones to divert traffic. The work is physical, done on site and with equipment.

The occupation's core duties are hands-on field work: clearing debris from culverts, ditches and drains, hauling material to fill washouts, and driving trucks to work sites. A software-only agent with no body cannot do any of these.

The typical entry route is a high school diploma plus moderate-term on-the-job training. No professional licence requires a human to sign off on debris removal itself, though heavy vehicles may need a CDL.

The only automation found for changing drill bits and loading bolts on roof bolters is mechanical: carousels and manipulators described in patents and controlled by machine controllers. That is robotics hardware, not a software agent, and on conventional machines operators still reload by hand.

Patents for autonomous roof bolters describe drilling and bolting sequences run by controllers and physical loading arms on the machine. A software-only AI with no body cannot do the physical work of pulling a bit from a chuck and seating a bolt underground.

A newer patent describes a controller that rotates the carousel to swap consumables such as drill bits, resin cartridges and bolts. This confirms the task is manual handling at the drill head in an underground mine.

AI drowning-detection systems such as Lynxight and AngelEye watch pool camera feeds and send alerts to lifeguards' smartwatches. They are presented as an extra layer of safety, not a replacement for lifeguards, and they only work at pools that already have the cameras installed.
Industry bodies treat AI drowning detection as a supplement to lifeguard supervision and are still working out how to fit it into existing supervision frameworks.
Florida law requires anyone working as a lifeguard at a public pool to hold a certificate from the American Red Cross, the YMCA, or another nationally recognized aquatic training program.

Zoos move animals between enclosures and into transport crates through hands-on shift and crate training led by keepers in person: targeting, positive reinforcement and handling the doors. That is physical work an agent without a body cannot do.
Moving an animal depends on keepers reading its behaviour on the spot and dealing with social or environmental problems, for example separating individuals or adding visual barriers.
Software such as Species360 ZIMS covers only the paperwork side: recording transfers and visits. An agent could help there, but that is a small part of the time the task takes.

Ticketing software can track exits and re-entries: scanning a ticket on the way out makes it valid again for coming back in, so the system does the record-keeping part of a door check. Staff still operate the scanner at the door.
For multi-day or high-volume events, vendors recommend physical credentials such as wristbands or hand stamps that staff check by eye at the door. That means a person has to be physically present.
At large venues, guests ask staff for a re-entry wristband when they leave and must show it with their ticket when they return.

Building a new bike from the box means handling the parts by hand: mounting wheels, seatpost, bar and stem, aligning the derailleur and brake calipers, and tightening bolts to spec with a torque wrench. An AI agent with no robot body can't do this. At most it can look up the manufacturer's instructions and torque specs.
Brake setup means holding the lever in while tightening the caliper bolts to 8 Nm, then spinning the wheel to check for rotor drag. These are hands-on adjust-and-check steps.

Under 16 CFR 1512.3, a bike sold partly assembled must meet federal safety requirements once it is put together according to the manufacturer's instructions. The rule sets a product standard and does not require a licensed or certified person to assemble it.

HR AI agents in 2026 handle recruiting (screening, scheduling), onboarding (provisioning, document tracking, FAQs) and performance (data aggregation, coaching nudges), with claimed cuts in HR admin time of up to 40% (vendor-reported).
About one in three organizations uses AI for first-round video or voice screening interviews, and AI scheduling tools reportedly cut coordinator time by 36%.

Postmasters recruit, interview, select, hire, train, supervise and evaluate post office staff, and select and train postmasters of associate units. This includes on-site on-the-job training and a final hiring decision made by an accountable manager.

The BLUPF90 suite is standard software for mixed-model analysis in animal breeding. It estimates variance components and heritability by REML, including standard errors, and it can be run from scripts, so an agent with code execution can do the core estimation.
UNE lab handouts show that AI-REML in blupf90+ reports standard errors for heritability and genetic correlations. This is a routine computational workflow.

bpf90tools is a Python wrapper built to automate breeding-value pipelines (renumf90, remlf90, airemlf90). The search found no turnkey end-to-end system, so a human still needs to choose the model and check the results.

NWCG Crew Boss (CRWB) qualification requires prior Firefighter Type 1 experience, a certified Position Task Book, specific courses (RT-130, S-230, S-290, ICS-200) and an arduous fitness level, so a qualified human must lead fire crews.
The CRWB role involves running, climbing and lifting over 50 lb, plus real-time decisions in the field, such as judging changing fire conditions and deciding when to withdraw a crew.

Digital tools such as VR forest-worker training and AI wildfire-planning platforms support training and planning, but they do not lead crews in the field. AI can only help with training materials, scheduling and briefings.

Commercial AI course-design tools available in 2026 (ibl.ai Course AI, Coursebox, Taskade) produce syllabi, weekly plans, learning objectives, rubrics and assignments from a course description, map content to accreditation outcomes and export to LMSs. These sources are vendor marketing with no independent quality data, and all of them assume a human reviews the output.

A 2025 case study describes a graduate course built quickly with generative AI to meet an accreditation deadline, including AI-generated syllabus, lecture and homework files. Faculty still had to direct and refine the work.

University governance gives faculty responsibility for curriculum. Course proposals start with a faculty member and pass through department, college and university committee approval. This is institutional governance, not a legal licence or signature requirement.

AI agent add-ons for Canvas can send scores straight to the Canvas gradebook through LTI grade passback. Canvas stays the official record for enrollment and grades, and other platforms already send session attendance to the gradebook automatically.
A news report says Instructure is rolling out an agentic AI assistant in Canvas that automates routine teaching work such as basic grading and rubric creation.

Nursing programs treat clinical evaluations and competency records as FERPA-protected education records. Access is limited to the course instructor and coordinators, so a human instructor stays responsible for certifying and controlling these records.
